stated: Reform UK will rebuild the UK fish processing industry through tax and other incentives to ensure that all fish caught in British waters are landed and processed in the UK, and by foreign vessels when capacity allows.

source.quote: Rebuild UK Fish Processing Tax and other incentives to ensure that all fish caught in British waters are landed and processed in the UK. Fish caught by foreign vessels in UK waters should also be landed and processed here when capacity allows.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets rebuilding the fish processing industry through incentives designed to create and retain domestic processing jobs — a direct, non-negligible effect on employment, job quality, and wages in coastal communities.
Rebuilding domestic processing capacity increases value-added industrial output, productivity and regional economic opportunity, affecting aggregate living standards in affected areas.
Fish processing employment is disproportionately concentrated in economically deprived coastal towns; restoring the industry would narrow regional income and opportunity gaps.
Tax and other incentives for the industry represent foregone public revenue, concretely worsening the funded/borrowed balance on the fiscal deficit indicator.

membership_note: This is an industrial-capacity and incentives policy with four real bearings: a direct labour-market effect (O4), an aggregate regional prosperity effect (O13), a regional-inequality narrowing effect (O14), and a public-finance cost from the tax incentives (O12). Environmental effects (O6) of increased domestic landing/processing are too indirect and unspecified to clear the non-negligible bar without knowing what environmental standards would apply.
